errors.issue: Reduced recovered product can also result from substrate sequestration/chemical loss or product destruction during target incubation. Post-quench product spikes and reporter transfer calibration do not exclude those alternatives; the design lacks time-matched substrate/product-plus-compound chemical controls.

errors.quote: Compound lowers target-product formation in a staged assay after reporter/detector calibration.
errors.issue: The following target-directed label should initially be target-step effect. The staged calibrated assay is an acceptable alternative in principle, but the missing chemical-fate controls prevent assignment to the enzyme itself.

errors.quote: This factor may reflect excitation absorption, fluorophore quenching, or another optical effect.
errors.issue: The enzyme-free fluorophore decrease may instead involve chemical conversion of the fluorescent species. The protocol does not independently establish fluorophore integrity.

errors.quote: Use when both affinity-like and maximal-rate effects are required by the data.
errors.issue: The standard-model branch lacks an inhibitor-depletion/tight-binding check and only lightly addresses time dependence. A validated range for free inhibitor and equilibration is needed before classifying mechanism.

rationale: Careful compound-specific reporter calibration, stopped target sampling, initial rates and a useful caution against binding-site inference. However, the plan repeatedly equates reduced product accumulation with direct enzyme inhibition while omitting chemical substrate/product loss controls. These are a substantial gap in the central discrimination; staged detection itself is not penalized.
reference_guardrails: D3 establishes spectral proximity, not the magnitude of inner filtering. Fluorophore-only signal loss does not distinguish absorption, quenching and chemical conversion.
Substrate-competitive inhibition is a kinetic subclass of target inhibition; it is not necessarily active-site occupancy. Substrate sequestration and chemical loss require separate controls.
Reporter-only inhibition and true target inhibition can coexist. Do not force mutually exclusive categories or subtract arbitrary effect percentages.

A fully validated staged reporter calibration can be informative; a specific analytical instrument is not mandatory. Target quenching, matrix matching, product recovery and chemical stability must justify the inference.
Orthogonal methods can have their own compound-dependent artifacts, including ion suppression. Nonfluorescence alone does not establish specificity.
Independent preparations/days support reproducibility; technical wells cannot substitute for them. A null significance test is not equivalence; margins should be scientifically justified.
Simple inner-filter correction formulas depend on optical geometry. For f=F_without/F_with, attenuation correction multiplies signal by f, not by 1/f.

The draft reference uses reporter Km as a preparation item, but full reporter Michaelis-Menten characterization is not universally essential if empirical capacity and relevant intermediate concentrations are validated.

No fixed concentrations, replicate counts, Z-prime or R-squared thresholds are supplied by the packet. Proposed pilot settings are acceptable when labeled and validated; they are not historical facts.
